correctness.rationale: A canonical dot-product incidence construction fixes all 21 edges. Seven-step recursive matching enumeration gives exactly 24 perfect matchings and independent Ryser permanent also gives 24. Comparing all 276 pairs yields exactly 178 distinct difference masks, size distribution 28/84/42/24. Full \(\binom{21}{6}=54{,}264\) enumeration finds 812 six-edge hexagon transversals; all miss a ten-edge symmetric difference. By monotonicity no set of six or fewer edges distinguishes all matchings. Full \(\binom{21}{7}=116{,}280\) enumeration finds 8,064 distinct-force edge sets, independently confirmed by matching-signature injectivity. Explicit witness 8795 establishes existence. Exactly 336 incidence automorphisms are generated and shown to preserve the matching family, and the resulting orbit partition exhausts 8064 sets in thirty orbits with stated sizes. All ranges finite/exhaustive, no timeout or extrapolation.

value.rationale: Global perfect-matching forcing is a natural minimum coordinate-separation invariant for the canonical Heawood cage, also a distinguished Pfaffian brace. Complete optimum multiplicity and orbit classification is a natural exhaustive invariant, not merely the known perfect-matching count. The five orbits of six-edge short-cycle transversals, each obstructed by longer nice decagons, explain why the attractive hexagon-only simplification fails. The 30 geometric symmetry types add structure to the scalar \(\operatorname{gf}(H)=7\) without claiming a larger general theorem.
